title: Lean proof — Ryser bounded n less equal 63 per D3 sketch
description:
Implement the Lean4 proof of Ryser's permanent formula correctness on the project's `FiniteField` trait, scoped to bounded $n \le 63$, per the approved D3 proof sketch.

## Background

D3's approved proof sketch (`4aaa6e4d`) bounds $n \le 63$ to fit within the single-`u64` subset enumeration regime; this avoids formalising arbitrary-arity sums (per the epic non-goal). The proof shows Ryser's permanent formula matches the standard (Mathlib) permanent definition, with the Gray-code walk traversing the subset lattice.

Same pipeline as V1; same verification-work conventions. **Final landing is the lead-approved Option 3 (Amendments §2, user-approved 2026-05-17): the abstract bounded-n Ryser correctness contract. Two consecutive gated extraction spikes empirically falsified binding the headline to extracted Rust on the pinned toolchain (evidence: `dev/active/0606186a-impl-handoff.md`); the extracted-Rust binding is descoped here and is instead delivered for the epic by V1 (`f05ffbe1`, closed — a [hard] Charon/Aeneas-extracted formal-verification deliverable).**

## Success Criteria

- [ ] [hard] `proofs/Gf2Algebra/Proofs/RyserBounded.lean` exists with the bounded-$n$ **abstract** Ryser correctness theorem — `ryser_permanent_bounded` ($\operatorname{ryserRHS}(\operatorname{matrixOfSlice} n\,M) = (\operatorname{matrixOfSlice} n\,M).\operatorname{permanent}$ over `ZMod 3`, carrying an explicit `n ≤ 63` hypothesis), built on `ryser_eq_permanent_zmod` (the Ryser identity over any `CommRing`) — and the proved Gray-code traversal-correctness lemmas (`subsetOfBits_bijective`, `gray_succ_xor`, `flipBit_lt`) establishing the Gray-walk ↔ powerset correspondence. (Amended 2026-05-17 from "the bounded-n Ryser correctness theorem and the Gray-code-walk loop invariant"; the *extracted-Rust* loop-invariant binding is descoped — see Amendments §2.)
- [ ] [hard] `cd proofs && lake build` succeeds with no `sorry` in the new file.
- [ ] [hard] V2's formal content is the abstract Ryser identity above (over `ZMod 3` / any `CommRing`, explicit `n ≤ 63`); the extracted-Rust binding to a monomorphised/generic `permanent_ryser` is **descoped** (twice-falsified at the Charon extraction layer — generic non-monomorphisation, then foreign-crate gfp-body skip; `dev/active/0606186a-impl-handoff.md`). The epic's [hard] Charon/Aeneas extracted-Rust formal-verification deliverable is provided by V1 `f05ffbe1` (closed). The now-purposeless V2 extraction scaffold `crates/gf2-algebra/src/permanent/ryser_fp3.rs` (a duplicate of generic `ryser.rs` with no production consumer) is removed to keep V2 SSOT-clean. (Amended 2026-05-17 from the prior "F_3 monomorphisation, test-certified bit-identical to generic T7" wording, itself amended from "targets the generic `permanent_ryser` (T7), not a copied stub"; see Amendments §2.)
- [ ] [hard] Bound $n \le 63$ is explicit in the theorem statement (`ryser_permanent_bounded`'s `(h_n : n ≤ 63)` hypothesis).
- [ ] [hard] `scripts/verify-lean.sh` regenerates LLBC + Lean from current Rust successfully (with the `ryser_fp3` extraction root removed; the committed `proofs/` tree is reproducible from current Rust).
- [ ] [hard] `lake-build` gate passes.

## Amendments (user-approved via project-lead escalation)

1. **(2026-05-17) Criterion 3 reworded** (first revision). From "targets the Rust production `permanent_ryser` (T7) generic over `FiniteField`, not a copied stub" → "targets the F_3 monomorphisation `permanent_ryser_fp3`, test-certified bit-identical to generic `permanent_ryser::<Fp<3>>`". **Reason:** the lead-approved Path-1 sketch §2 option-(b) (thin delegation so Charon monomorphises the generic) was empirically falsified by the gated extraction spike — Charon `1ec8d4bb` does not monomorphise a generic from a non-generic `--start-from` root; Aeneas emits `sorry` into the proof target's signature (`type_var_id … ExtractBase.Item`, `ryser.rs:152-163`). *(Superseded by §2.)*

2. **(2026-05-17) Criteria 1 & 3 amended to the abstract-only contract (Option 3, user-selected).** The second gated spike (Option-2 / C3) showed the *transparent-gfp prerequisite itself* is infeasible on the pinned toolchain: in the gf2_algebra Charon leg, `gf2-core` is a foreign dependency crate and Charon skips foreign-method bodies by default; `--opaque`/`--start-from` do not override this, and the only flag that would (`--extract-opaque-bodies`, global) fatally panics rustc on std/core. So the `Fp<3>` arithmetic is uninterpreted in that leg regardless of flags — no path to the extracted-Rust headline without a shared-infrastructure Charon change. The user selected Option 3: land V2 on the proved sorry-free abstract Ryser contract (`ryser_permanent_bounded`, explicit `n ≤ 63`), descope the extracted-Rust binding, and remove the now-purposeless `ryser_fp3.rs` extraction scaffold (no production consumer; duplicated `ryser.rs` — its removal resolves the prior code-review SSOT finding). V1 `f05ffbe1` (closed) remains the epic's [hard] extracted-Rust formal-verification deliverable. Selected by the user over (1) a 5th shared-infra Charon patch, (2) a third-leg gf2-core import with TypesExternal-collision merge, and (4) pausing for user-led Charon investigation. Full mechanism-level evidence: `dev/active/0606186a-impl-handoff.md`.
